headline: Whitewater and Wild Peak Reservations
reservation: For Arkansas River activities, check the Bureau of Land Management and Colorado Parks and Wildlife for river access permits. Guided rafting trips through Browns Canyon and high-altitude lodging in town require months of lead time for summer; confirm current systems directly with official agencies.

days.title: Arkansas River and Downtown Pulse

stops.name: Browns Canyon National Monument
stops.detail: Experience the rugged granite walls and class III rapids that define the Arkansas River corridor.

stops.name: Salida Riverside Park
stops.detail: Observe local kayakers at the F Street play hole and stroll the historic downtown riverfront.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; conditions vary by canyon traffic
days.note: Water levels peak during June runoff; always verify current river CFS (cubic feet per second) before entry.

days.title: Collegiate Peaks and High Alpine Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 7:00 AM from a local Salida lodge

stops.name: Monarch Pass
stops.detail: Ascend the Continental Divide for panoramic views of the Sawatch Range and high-altitude hiking.

stops.name: Mount Shavano
stops.detail: A prominent peak offering technical hiking for experienced mountaineers with views of the valley floor.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; conditions vary on high-altitude passes
days.note: Thunderstorms are common in the afternoons; plan to be below the treeline by noon.

days.title: Geothermal Soaks and Ghost Town History

stops.name: Mount Princeton Hot Springs
stops.detail: Soak in natural geothermal pools set against the backdrop of towering white granite peaks.

stops.name: St. Elmo Ghost Town
stops.detail: Visit one of Colorado's best-preserved mining towns to see historic wooden structures and local wildlife.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; conditions vary on gravel sections near St. Elmo
days.note: Roads to historic sites may be narrow; check for seasonal closures after early autumn snow.

intel.title: Downtown Salida Access
intel.text: F Street parking fills quickly on summer weekends during the Riverside Music Festival. Utilize designated public lots two blocks east of the river park to avoid congestion.

intel.title: Wilderness Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is reliable in Salida and Buena Vista but drops immediately upon entering the San Isabel National Forest. Download digital maps before heading toward Monarch Pass or the Chalk Creek area.

intel.title: Valley Refueling
intel.text: Reliable fuel services are concentrated along Highway 50 and Highway 24. Ensure your tank is full before venturing onto the remote forest service roads leading to Fourteeners.

intel.title: Peak Season Planning
intel.text: July and August bring the highest visitor volume for rafting and hiking. Consider September for stable weather and gold aspen foliage with fewer crowds.

intel.title: Forest Road Conditions
intel.text: Many trailheads require high-clearance vehicles to navigate rocky washouts. Check the Salida Ranger District website for current road status and seasonal gate closures.

plan.arrival: Arrive via Gunnison Crested Butte Regional Airport (GUC), pick up a rental vehicle, and head east on Highway 50. Stop in Salida for grocery supplies before checking into your mountain cabin or yurt.
plan.vehicle: A high-clearance 4WD vehicle is recommended for forest road access; check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved surfaces.
plan.goldenHour: Tenderfoot Mountain (S Mountain) offers a view of the town under the glow of the Sawatch Range, best at sunset in late summer.
